attractions.name: Central Park
attractions.desc: 843 acres of free. Nap on a rock, people-watch by the pond, pretend the rent around you isn't $4k.

attractions.name: Brooklyn Bridge
attractions.desc: Walk it at 2 AM when it's just you, the cables, and a skyline that owes you nothing. Costs zero.

attractions.name: Times Square
attractions.desc: A million watts of ads screaming at you for free. Once in your life, be the person standing still in it.

attractions.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
attractions.desc: Five thousand years of humanity under one roof. Get lost until they kick you out at closing.

attractions.name: Statue of Liberty
attractions.desc: The ferry ride alone is worth it — salt air, harbor wind, and the green lady getting bigger and bigger.

attractions.name: Empire State Building
attractions.desc: Yes it's touristy. Yes you'll stand at the top at night and feel like the main character anyway.

attractions.name: The High Line
attractions.desc: An old train line turned sky garden. Float above the traffic for thirty blocks without spending a dime.

attractions.name: Chelsea Market
attractions.desc: Free to wander, dangerous to smell. Window-shop the tacos and lobster rolls until payday hits.

attractions.name: MoMA
attractions.desc: Stand in front of Starry Night and let it fix something in you. Worth every saved-up dollar.

attractions.name: Griffith Observatory
attractions.desc: Free telescopes, free skyline, free existential moment over the whole glittering basin. Go at dusk.

attractions.name: Venice Beach Boardwalk
attractions.desc: Muscle beach, street performers, ocean haze. The weirdest free show in America, daily.

attractions.name: Santa Monica Pier
attractions.desc: Where Route 66 runs out of road. The ferris wheel lights hit different when you're broke and dreaming.

attractions.name: Hollywood Sign Hike
attractions.desc: Sweat your way up to nine white letters and a view that explains why everyone keeps moving here.

attractions.name: The Getty Center
attractions.desc: A billion-dollar hilltop art palace with free admission. The tram ride up feels like winning something.

attractions.name: Grand Central Market
attractions.desc: A century of downtown eating under one neon roof. Walk every stall twice before committing your $8.

attractions.name: The Broad
attractions.desc: Free contemporary art in a honeycomb spaceship. Book ahead and act like you always do this.

attractions.name: Runyon Canyon
attractions.desc: LA's unofficial dog park slash outdoor gym. Come for the trail, stay for the golden-hour city views.

attractions.name: Hollywood Walk of Fame
attractions.desc: Stars underfoot for miles, zero dollars. Find your favorite name and take the picture. It's the law.

attractions.name: LACMA
attractions.desc: The glowing lamppost forest outside is free forever. The art inside is your treat-yourself day.

attractions.name: British Museum
attractions.desc: The entire ancient world, admission zero. Rosetta Stone before lunch, mummies after. Rain-proof too.

attractions.name: Borough Market
attractions.desc: A thousand years of market under the railway arches. Free samples if you make eye contact bravely.

attractions.name: Tate Modern
attractions.desc: World-class art in an old power station, free. The Thames view from the top floor is the encore.

attractions.name: Hyde Park
attractions.desc: Royal grass, rentable deck chairs, swans with attitude. Bring a sandwich, own the afternoon.

attractions.name: Tower Bridge
attractions.desc: Walking across the fancy blue one costs nothing and photographs like a movie set. Go at blue hour.

attractions.name: Camden Market
attractions.desc: Punk leftovers, canal-side food stalls, and stuff you didn't know you wanted. Browsing is free therapy.

attractions.name: Buckingham Palace
attractions.desc: Stand at the gates and judge the guards' hats for free. The King will not be checking your bank balance.

attractions.name: Primrose Hill
attractions.desc: One short climb, the whole skyline laid out like a postcard you didn't have to buy.

attractions.name: Tower of London
attractions.desc: A thousand years of drama, ravens on payroll, and the actual Crown Jewels. Someday-splurge material.

attractions.name: London Eye
attractions.desc: Thirty slow minutes above the Thames in a glass pod. Save it for someone worth the ticket.

attractions.name: Senso-ji Temple
attractions.desc: Tokyo's oldest temple, incense smoke, a giant red lantern. Free fortunes for 100 yen if you're feeling lucky.

attractions.name: Shibuya Crossing
attractions.desc: Three thousand people scramble every light change. Cross it once, then watch from above like a movie.

attractions.name: Meiji Shrine
attractions.desc: A forest swallows the city ten steps past the torii gate. The quietest free reset in Tokyo.

attractions.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
attractions.desc: Knife shops, tamagoyaki on sticks, tuna sellers yelling at dawn. Come hungry, leave broke but happy.

attractions.name: Ueno Park
attractions.desc: Museums, temples, and in spring the cherry-blossom party of your dreams. The lawn seats are free forever.

attractions.name: Takeshita Street
attractions.desc: Harajuku's sugar-rush alley: crepes, chaos, fashion from the future. Window-shopping is the whole sport.

attractions.name: Tokyo Skytree
attractions.desc: 634 meters up, the city dissolves into circuit-board infinity. Night tickets are the someday move.

attractions.name: Tokyo Tower
attractions.desc: The orange original. Cheaper than Skytree, twice the retro romance, glows like a promise after dark.

attractions.name: Shinjuku Gyoen
attractions.desc: Three gardens in one for pocket change. The lawn under the plane trees fixes whatever's wrong with you.

attractions.name: teamLab Planets
attractions.desc: Wade barefoot through rooms made of light and water. The one splurge that turns your camera roll unreal.

attractions.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
attractions.desc: A whole royal palace for the price of a coffee. Rent a hanbok and they wave you in for free.

attractions.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
attractions.desc: Tiled-roof lanes where old Seoul still lives. Whisper-quiet, camera-ready, completely free.

attractions.name: Gwangjang Market
attractions.desc: Bindaetteok sizzling since 1905. Squeeze onto a stool, point at things, live your street-food dream.

attractions.name: N Seoul Tower
attractions.desc: The love-lock tower on the mountain. Hike up free, pay only if you want the observatory glow-up.

attractions.name: Banpo Hangang Park
attractions.desc: Riverside picnic culture at its peak: delivery chicken, convenience-store ramyeon, rainbow bridge fountain.

attractions.name: Myeongdong Shopping Street
attractions.desc: Neon canyon of skincare, snacks, and street grills. Browsing costs nothing; willpower costs everything.

attractions.name: Changdeokgung Secret Garden
attractions.desc: A hidden royal garden behind a palace, tour-only and worth every won. Autumn here is a personality reset.

attractions.name: Seoul Sky at Lotte World Tower
attractions.desc: Glass floor on the 118th floor of Korea's tallest building. Save it for the day you feel invincible.

attractions.name: Hongdae Street
attractions.desc: Buskers, dance crews, and midnight energy that never asks for a cover charge. Seoul's free main stage.

attractions.name: Namsan Park Trails
attractions.desc: A mountain in the middle of the city, stairs and all. Sunrise up top costs nothing but your sleep schedule.

attractions.name: Zócalo
attractions.desc: A plaza so huge your rent worries feel small. Flag ceremonies, Aztec drummers, centuries stacked under your sneakers — zero pesos.

attractions.name: Bosque de Chapultepec
attractions.desc: Twice the size of Central Park, infinitely cheaper. Nap by the lake, dodge squirrels, pretend the castle on the hill is yours.

attractions.name: Museo Nacional de Antropología
attractions.desc: The Aztec sun stone lives here and a ticket costs less than your delivery fees. Save it for a rainy someday afternoon.

attractions.name: Museo Frida Kahlo (Casa Azul)
attractions.desc: The blue house that launched a billion tote bags. Book ahead, cry a little, leave inspired and pleasantly broke.

attractions.name: Teotihuacán
attractions.desc: Pyramids older than the Aztecs, an hour from the city. Entry costs less than a latte; the goosebumps are complimentary.

attractions.name: Xochimilco Trajineras
attractions.desc: Rent a rainbow boat, split it eight ways, drift past floating mariachis with snacks in reach. Chaotic, floral, unbeatable.

attractions.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes
attractions.desc: Orange dome, marble everything, Rivera murals upstairs. Loiter outside for free; the inside costs pocket change.

attractions.name: Torre Latinoamericana
attractions.desc: Ride up 44 floors and watch the megacity blink to the horizon in every direction. Cheaper than therapy, better lighting.

attractions.name: Mercado de Coyoacán
attractions.desc: Tostadas the size of your ambitions in Frida's old neighborhood. Come hungry, leave broke in the best possible way.

attractions.name: Templo Mayor
attractions.desc: Aztec ruins hiding beside the cathedral like the city forgot to mention them. Entry: pocket change. Perspective: enormous.

attractions.name: Eiffel Tower
attractions.desc: Yes, it's a cliché. It's also 330 meters of sparkle every hour after dark — and the lawn view is free until you can afford the summit.

attractions.name: Louvre Museum
attractions.desc: A palace stuffed with 35,000 artworks. The Mona Lisa is tiny; the ego boost of finally going is enormous. Wear comfy shoes.

attractions.name: Sacré-Cœur Basilica
attractions.desc: Climb Montmartre's steps, wander in for free, and watch all of Paris pretend to be a postcard below your feet.

attractions.name: Musée d'Orsay
attractions.desc: Van Gogh and Monet living inside a gorgeous old train station. That giant clock window is the photo you've been saving up for.

attractions.name: Jardin du Luxembourg
attractions.desc: Free chairs by the fountain, toy sailboats, chess grandpas. Grab a baguette and live your best six-euro afternoon.

attractions.name: Canal Saint-Martin
attractions.desc: Iron footbridges, cheap wine on the quay, locals doing absolutely nothing beautifully. Your future picnic headquarters.

attractions.name: Père Lachaise Cemetery
attractions.desc: The world's most famous cemetery: Wilde, Piaf, Morrison. Gothic, leafy, free, and weirdly peaceful at golden hour.

attractions.name: Marché des Enfants Rouges
attractions.desc: Paris's oldest market, tucked in the Marais since 1615. Eat your way from Morocco to Japan for the price of one museum ticket.

attractions.name: Arc de Triomphe
attractions.desc: Climb 284 steps for the view the Eiffel can't give you: the Eiffel itself, plus twelve avenues spinning like a compass.

attractions.name: Sainte-Chapelle
attractions.desc: A 13th-century jewel box where the walls are basically all stained glass. Go on a sunny day and let it wreck you.

attractions.name: Brandenburg Gate
attractions.desc: The gate that watched empires, walls, and raves come and go. Costs nothing, means everything, open 24/7 like the city.

attractions.name: East Side Gallery
attractions.desc: 1.3 km of the actual Berlin Wall, painted by artists from everywhere. The world's longest open-air gallery; admission is a stroll.

attractions.name: Reichstag Dome
attractions.desc: A glass spiral above parliament with a free 360° of the whole city. Book ahead online — democracy's best free viewpoint.

attractions.name: Museum Island
attractions.desc: Five museums crowded onto one river island — Nefertiti lives here. Pick one, pay pocket money, feel cultured for a week.

attractions.name: Tempelhofer Feld
attractions.desc: An entire retired airport turned public park. Bike the runways, grill the infield, fly kites past the terminal. Peak Berlin, perfectly free.

attractions.name: Mauerpark Flea Market
attractions.desc: Sunday flea market plus open-air karaoke in a stone amphitheater. Strangers will cheer your worst singing. Free therapy.

attractions.name: Fernsehturm (TV Tower)
attractions.desc: The disco-ball-on-a-stick from every Berlin postcard. Someday: sunset from 203 meters. Until then it's your free compass home.

attractions.name: Tiergarten
attractions.desc: Berlin's green lung between the Gate and the zoo. Beer gardens hide among the trees; so do nude sunbathers. You've been warned.

attractions.name: Berlin Wall Memorial
attractions.desc: The stretch of Bernauer Strasse where the Wall's whole story is told, free and unflinching. Heavy, necessary, unforgettable.

attractions.name: Checkpoint Charlie
attractions.desc: The Cold War's most famous border booth, now surrounded by döner shops. Kitschy? Yes. Still gives chills? Also yes.

attractions.name: Grand Palace
attractions.desc: Gold on gold on gold — it glitters so hard sunglasses count as gear. Save up; this is Bangkok's crown jewel, literally.

attractions.name: Wat Pho
attractions.desc: Home of the 46-meter reclining Buddha whose feet alone are artworks. Also the birthplace of Thai massage. Bliss on a budget.

attractions.name: Wat Arun
attractions.desc: The riverside spire that owns every Bangkok sunset. Cross by ferry for pennies, climb the steep steps, feel epic.

attractions.name: Chatuchak Weekend Market
attractions.desc: Fifteen thousand stalls of things you never knew you needed. Entry is free; leaving with an empty wallet is a personal choice.

attractions.name: Lumphini Park
attractions.desc: Bangkok's green escape, patrolled by giant monitor lizards that fear absolutely nothing. Free aerobics at dusk if you're brave.

attractions.name: Khao San Road
attractions.desc: Backpacker Broadway: bucket drinks, pad thai carts, questionable tattoos. You come to people-watch; you stay till 3 a.m.

attractions.name: Jim Thompson House
attractions.desc: A silk tycoon's teakwood house-museum wrapped in jungle garden. He vanished mysteriously; the calm here never does.

attractions.name: Yaowarat (Chinatown)
attractions.desc: Neon canyons and sidewalk woks after dark. The best meal of your life is under three dollars here — the hard part is choosing.

attractions.name: Mahanakhon SkyWalk
attractions.desc: A glass floor 78 stories up, for standing over Bangkok like you own it. Someday-splurge material; screenshot the skyline till then.

attractions.name: Sydney Opera House
attractions.desc: The sails you've doodled in every notebook margin. Walking the forecourt costs nothing; the smug harbour glow is included.

attractions.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
attractions.desc: Walk the Coathanger for free and pocket the postcard view. The paid climb can wait for richer, braver future-you.

attractions.name: Bondi to Coogee Coastal Walk
attractions.desc: Six clifftop kilometers of surf, sea pools, and salt air. Costs nothing but calf muscles. Bring water and main-character energy.

attractions.name: Royal Botanic Garden
attractions.desc: Harbour-front gardens where cockatoos photobomb your lunch. Free, gorgeous, and the Opera House poses for you at the gate.

attractions.name: Manly Beach
attractions.desc: Catch the ferry across the harbour — cheap thrill, million-dollar views — to a beach town that runs on salt and sunscreen.

attractions.name: Taronga Zoo
attractions.desc: Giraffes with a better harbour view than any penthouse. A proper splurge, but the ferry ride over is half the magic.

attractions.name: Art Gallery of New South Wales
attractions.desc: A grand gallery on the park's edge — old masters, bold new wings, zero dollars. Your rainy-day cheat code.

attractions.name: Sydney Fish Market
attractions.desc: Watch the trawlers unload, then demolish a seafood platter on the wharf while seagulls plot against you.

attractions.name: Darling Harbour
attractions.desc: A waterfront loop of lights, buskers, and Saturday fireworks that cost you exactly nothing. Date-night training wheels.

attractions.name: Queen Victoria Building
attractions.desc: A cathedral built for shopping: stained glass, mosaic floors, a giant hanging clock. Window-shop like royalty for free.

attractions.name: CN Tower
attractions.desc: 553m of pure vertigo. The glass floor dares you; your knees decline. Skyline for days once you peel off the wall.

attractions.name: Toronto Islands
attractions.desc: A cheap ferry buys the city's best skyline, beaches, and zero cars. Cheapest 'I left town' feeling money can buy.

attractions.name: St. Lawrence Market
attractions.desc: Peameal bacon sandwich HQ since forever. Wander the stalls, eat with your eyes for free, budget for the bun.

attractions.name: High Park
attractions.desc: Cherry blossoms in spring, a free little zoo with capybaras, trails forever. Toronto's backyard, no cover charge.

attractions.name: Royal Ontario Museum
attractions.desc: Dinosaurs behind a crystal that crash-landed on a heritage building. Wait for discount nights, roar responsibly.

attractions.name: Casa Loma
attractions.desc: An actual castle a rich guy built and then couldn't afford. Relatable. The secret tunnel earns the ticket.

attractions.name: Art Gallery of Ontario
attractions.desc: Gehry staircase, Group of Seven forests. Under-25s get in free — flash that fading youth while it lasts.

attractions.name: Distillery District
attractions.desc: Cobblestones, old whisky warehouses, twinkle lights. Free to wander, dangerous to window-shop.

attractions.name: Kensington Market
attractions.desc: Vintage racks, patties, murals, someone playing a saw. The city's weird heart — admission: nothing.

attractions.name: Ripley's Aquarium of Canada
attractions.desc: A moving walkway under sharks. Pricey, but the glowing jelly room is basically free therapy... after the ticket.

attractions.name: Cloud Gate (The Bean)
attractions.desc: Chicago's giant chrome bean. Free funhouse mirror, mandatory selfie, your reflection warped into modern art.

attractions.name: Art Institute of Chicago
attractions.desc: Lions out front, Seurat's dots inside. One ticket, several centuries. Ferris Bueller stared here; so will you.

attractions.name: Willis Tower Skydeck
attractions.desc: Step onto a glass ledge 103 floors up and reconsider your choices. Four states visible on a clear day.

attractions.name: Navy Pier
attractions.desc: Free to stroll, ferris wheel extra. Lake breeze, summer fireworks, tourist chaos that somehow charms.

attractions.name: Lincoln Park Zoo
attractions.desc: One of America's last free zoos. Lions for the price of nothing. The ultimate broke-day royalty move.

attractions.name: Chicago Riverwalk
attractions.desc: Walk between skyscrapers at water level while architecture boats narrate overhead. Your feet are the free tour.

attractions.name: Field Museum
attractions.desc: Home of Sue, the internet's sassiest T. rex. Acres of dead things that feel extremely alive.

attractions.name: Wrigley Field
attractions.desc: Century-old ivy walls. Bleacher seats on a losing streak cost less than a deep dish — that's the move.

attractions.name: Garfield Park Conservatory
attractions.desc: Landscape art under glass — a free indoor jungle for when the lake wind gets personal in January.

attractions.name: Gardens by the Bay
attractions.desc: Supertrees glow for free every night; the cloud-forest dome charges. Sci-fi botany either way.

attractions.name: Marina Bay Sands SkyPark
attractions.desc: A surfboard balanced on three towers. Pool is guests-only, but the deck view still bankrupts your camera roll.

attractions.name: Merlion Park
attractions.desc: Half lion, half fish, forever spitting into the bay. Free photo with the city's weirdest mascot.

attractions.name: Singapore Botanic Gardens
attractions.desc: A UNESCO garden older than the country, free at dawn tai-chi hour. The orchid wing costs about a coffee.

attractions.name: Singapore Zoo
attractions.desc: Orangutans take breakfast beside you, barely a cage in sight. Save up — it's the good kind of splurge.

attractions.name: Night Safari
attractions.desc: The world's first nocturnal zoo. Tram through the dark while leopards silently judge your life.

attractions.name: Maxwell Food Centre
attractions.desc: Michelin-listed chicken rice for pocket change. The hawker dream: queue, feast, repeat.

attractions.name: Haw Par Villa
attractions.desc: A free, gloriously unhinged statue park of Chinese legends, Ten Courts of Hell included. Sleep well.

attractions.name: Jewel Changi Rain Vortex
attractions.desc: A 40-metre indoor waterfall inside an airport. Go for the mist, stay because your flight's delayed anyway.

attractions.name: East Coast Park
attractions.desc: 15km of beach, BBQ pits and rental bikes. Sunset satay by the sea costs less than a movie ticket.

attractions.name: Space Center Houston
attractions.desc: Touch a moon rock, tour real Mission Control. 'Houston' means this place. Save up — it's worth the launch.

attractions.name: Buffalo Bayou Park
attractions.desc: Skyline views, a bat colony at dusk, kayaks under the towers. Free therapy with mosquito DLC.

attractions.name: The Menil Collection
attractions.desc: World-class art, permanently free, hiding in leafy Montrose. The Rothko Chapel next door will rewire you.

attractions.name: Houston Museum of Natural Science
attractions.desc: Dinos downstairs, a gem vault that makes rappers jealous. Hunt the free-hours window like a raptor.

attractions.name: Museum of Fine Arts, Houston
attractions.desc: Two buildings joined by a glowing light tunnel, plus free Thursdays. The tunnel selfie is a rite of passage.

attractions.name: Houston Zoo
attractions.desc: Giraffe feeding for a few bucks extra — lettuce from your hand, mild judgment from their eyes.

attractions.name: Discovery Green
attractions.desc: Downtown's front lawn: free concerts, an ice rink in 'winter', food trucks circling like friendly sharks.

attractions.name: Gerald D. Hines Waterwall Park
attractions.desc: A 64-foot horseshoe of falling water. Free mist facial, engagement-photo magnet, weirdly hypnotic.

attractions.name: Kemah Boardwalk
attractions.desc: Gulf-side rides and seafood a short drive out. Walking the boards is free; the wooden coaster will taunt you.

attractions.name: Golden Gate Bridge
attractions.desc: Walk 1.7 miles of international orange through fog that arrives like clockwork. Free, iconic, bring a windproof soul.

attractions.name: Alcatraz Island
attractions.desc: The Rock: a ferry, a haunted cellblock, an audio tour by former guards. Book weeks out; escape attempts extra.

attractions.name: Golden Gate Park
attractions.desc: Bigger than Central Park, with bison. Actual bison. Free roaming for you; they're the ones fenced in.

attractions.name: Pier 39
attractions.desc: Sea lions took over a dock in 1989 and never left. The loudest free comedy show in town.

attractions.name: Cable Cars
attractions.desc: Hang off the running board of a moving national landmark for eight bucks. Hills drop away like a movie shot.

attractions.name: Ferry Building Marketplace
attractions.desc: Saturday farmers market outside, oysters and sourdough inside. Sample your way to a free-ish lunch.

attractions.name: Lands End
attractions.desc: Cliff trails, shipwreck views, the ruins of Sutro Baths. Feels like the edge of the world because it is.

attractions.name: Palace of Fine Arts
attractions.desc: A Roman ruin built on purpose in 1915, ringed by swans. The most proposal-photographed rotunda in the West.

attractions.name: Twin Peaks
attractions.desc: Huff up for the full 360° city sparkle. Bring a hoodie; Karl the Fog attends most evenings.

attractions.name: Coit Tower
attractions.desc: Depression-era murals downstairs are free; the elevator view costs a burrito. Climb the Filbert Steps to earn it.

attractions.name: Jackson Square
attractions.desc: Artists, fortune tellers, and a cathedral photobombing every shot. Costs nothing, feels like the center of the universe at midnight.

attractions.name: St. Louis Cathedral
attractions.desc: That triple-spired postcard you have already screenshotted. Step inside for free and let the AC and the hush do their thing.

attractions.name: National WWII Museum
attractions.desc: A whole campus of history that eats an entire day. Pricey, yes, but this is the splurge you plan around for months.

attractions.name: City Park
attractions.desc: Ancient oaks dripping with moss, bigger than Central Park, and free. Bring the dog and a daydream, leave with both happier.

attractions.name: Frenchmen Street
attractions.desc: Live jazz spills out of every doorway after dark. Wandering the sidewalk with zero dollars is a legitimate concert ticket here.

attractions.name: Preservation Hall
attractions.desc: A tiny wooden room where jazz gets played the old way, no phones, no drinks, all goosebumps. Worth skipping lunches for.

attractions.name: St. Charles Streetcar
attractions.desc: A dollar and a quarter buys you a rattling mansion tour under the oaks. Cheapest time machine in America.

attractions.name: French Market
attractions.desc: Open-air stalls of hot sauce, trinkets, and snacks by the river. Browse hungry, leave with exactly one weird treasure.

attractions.name: Crescent Park
attractions.desc: A rusty-chic riverside walk where the Mississippi bends and the skyline glows. Free front-row seats to barge-watching.

attractions.name: Garden District Stroll
attractions.desc: Self-guided mansion envy under live oaks. Pick your future house, argue about paint colors, spend nothing.

attractions.name: Templo de Santo Domingo
attractions.desc: A baroque church so gold inside it feels illegal to see for free. Sunset on the plaza out front is the daily main event.

attractions.name: Monte Albán
attractions.desc: Zapotec pyramids on a flattened mountaintop with valley views forever. Five bucks to stand on top of 2,500 years.

attractions.name: Hierve el Agua
attractions.desc: A petrified waterfall with infinity pools carved by minerals, not influencers. Pack snacks, the view does the rest.

attractions.name: Árbol del Tule
attractions.desc: A 2,000-year-old tree so wide it makes buses look shy. One dollar to feel very small in the best way.

attractions.name: Jardín Etnobotánico
attractions.desc: Cacti arranged like sculpture behind old convent walls. The guided walk is the price of a fancy coffee and twice as calming.

attractions.name: Zócalo de Oaxaca
attractions.desc: Marimba bands, balloon sellers, and free people-watching under the laurels. The city's living room, open all night.

attractions.name: Mercado 20 de Noviembre
attractions.desc: The famous smoke hall where grilled meat clouds guide you like a beacon. Entry free, willpower not included.

attractions.name: Andador Calle Alcalá
attractions.desc: A cobbled pedestrian street of green stone buildings and gallery windows. Walk it slow, twice, for zero pesos.

attractions.name: Mitla
attractions.desc: Geometric stone mosaics older than your entire family tree. A quiet day trip that costs less than lunch.

attractions.name: Malecón de Miraflores
attractions.desc: Clifftop paths where paragliders float past and the Pacific hums below. The best free therapy session in Lima.

attractions.name: Parque del Amor
attractions.desc: A giant kissing statue, mosaic benches, ocean sunsets. Bring someone, or just bring headphones and feelings.

attractions.name: Huaca Pucllana
attractions.desc: A pre-Inca pyramid casually parked between apartment blocks. Five bucks to time-travel without leaving Miraflores.

attractions.name: Plaza Mayor de Lima
attractions.desc: Yellow colonial facades, palace guards, pigeon drama. The city's origin point, still free after 500 years.

attractions.name: Museo Larco
attractions.desc: Gold, ceramics, and a bougainvillea courtyard that looks rented for weddings. The one museum splurge everyone defends.

attractions.name: Circuito Mágico del Agua
attractions.desc: Laser-lit fountains you can run through for pocket change. Peak cheap-date engineering.

attractions.name: Puente de los Suspiros
attractions.desc: Barranco's wooden bridge of sighs. Legend says hold your breath crossing and wish. Wishes are still free.

attractions.name: Monasterio de San Francisco
attractions.desc: A gorgeous convent with bone-stacked catacombs underneath. Four dollars for a library upstairs and skulls downstairs.

attractions.name: Parque Kennedy
attractions.desc: The famous plaza where dozens of cats hold court among churro carts. Free admission, priceless committee of cats.

attractions.name: Mercado de Surquillo
attractions.desc: Where Lima's chefs shop at dawn: mountains of ají, fruit you cannot pronounce, fish still bragging about the ocean.

attractions.name: Cementerio de la Recoleta
attractions.desc: A marble city of the dead where Evita rests and cats patrol the alleys. Gothic, gorgeous, worth the ticket.

attractions.name: Caminito
attractions.desc: La Boca's candy-colored tin houses with tango dancers working the corners. Loudest free photo op in South America.

attractions.name: Teatro Colón
attractions.desc: One of the world's great opera houses. Take the tour now, promise yourself the box seats later.

attractions.name: Plaza de Mayo
attractions.desc: The pink palace, the mothers' scarves painted on stone, two centuries of history in one free square.

attractions.name: Feria de San Telmo
attractions.desc: Sunday antiques stretching for blocks: old soda siphons, tango vinyl, street bands. Browsing is the whole sport.

attractions.name: Bosques de Palermo
attractions.desc: Lakes, rose gardens, and rollerbladers who never miss. Rent nothing, walk everything, spend zero.

attractions.name: El Ateneo Grand Splendid
attractions.desc: A century-old theater reborn as a bookstore, café on the stage. Free to enter, dangerous for book budgets.

attractions.name: Puente de la Mujer
attractions.desc: Puerto Madero's white swoosh of a bridge, best at dusk when the docks glow. A free skyline moment.

attractions.name: MALBA
attractions.desc: Latin American art heavyweights in a bright modern box. The kind of ten dollars that upgrades your whole personality.

attractions.name: Obelisco
attractions.desc: The needle in the middle of the widest avenue on earth. Stand there once at night, honking traffic and all. Free forever.

attractions.name: Parque Ibirapuera
attractions.desc: São Paulo's green lung: lakes, museums, joggers, capybara rumors. A full free Sunday, batteries included.

attractions.name: Avenida Paulista
attractions.desc: On Sundays the skyscraper canyon closes to cars and fills with buskers and dogs in sweaters. Peak free Sampa.

attractions.name: MASP
attractions.desc: The red-legged icon floating over Paulista, paintings hung on glass like they levitate. Save up, then linger for hours.

attractions.name: Mercadão Municipal
attractions.desc: Stained-glass market famous for absurd mortadella sandwiches and fruit sellers who insist you try everything.

attractions.name: Beco do Batman
attractions.desc: An open-air alley gallery in Vila Madalena where the murals change before your feed does. Zero reais, all color.

attractions.name: Bairro da Liberdade
attractions.desc: Red lanterns over the largest Japanese community outside Japan. Window-shop snacks now, feast someday.

attractions.name: Pinacoteca de São Paulo
attractions.desc: Brazilian art in a sunlit brick palace by the old train station. Six bucks, and free some days if you time it right.

attractions.name: Farol Santander
attractions.desc: Ride up an old bank tower to watch the city's endless skyline blur into the horizon. Vertigo, but make it romantic.

attractions.name: Catedral da Sé
attractions.desc: A huge neo-gothic cathedral at kilometer zero of the megacity. Free to enter, impossible to fit in one photo.

attractions.name: Theatro Municipal
attractions.desc: A gilded opera house straight out of Paris envy. Tours cost pocket change; the chandelier gawking is free with it.

attractions.name: Colosseum
attractions.desc: Gladiators fought here for free; you'll pay about $20 to stand where they did. Worth every cent of the someday fund.

attractions.name: Trevi Fountain
attractions.desc: Toss a coin, guarantee your return trip — cheapest travel insurance on Earth. Go after midnight when the crowds finally sleep.

attractions.name: Pantheon
attractions.desc: A 2,000-year-old concrete dome with a hole in the roof, still flexing on modern architects. A few bucks to stand under the sky.

attractions.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
attractions.desc: Miles of papal loot ending under Michelangelo's ceiling. Your neck will ache. Your soul won't.

attractions.name: St. Peter's Basilica
attractions.desc: The biggest church flex in Christendom and it costs nothing to walk in. Dress code strict, awe unlimited.

attractions.name: Villa Borghese Gardens
attractions.desc: Rome's green rooftop — rent nothing, wander everything, and spy on the skyline from the Pincio ledge for zero euros.

attractions.name: Spanish Steps
attractions.desc: 135 steps of prime people-watching. Sitting's banned now, so strike a pose and pretend you're in a 60s film.

attractions.name: Campo de' Fiori Market
attractions.desc: Tomatoes and gossip by morning; by night the square swaps produce for spritz. Both shows are free to watch.

attractions.name: Gianicolo Hill
attractions.desc: Climb above Trastevere at sunset and watch every dome in Rome blush. A cannon fires at noon; your jaw drops for free.

attractions.name: Roman Forum
attractions.desc: Downtown of the ancient world, now a gorgeous pile of rubble you can stroll through. Emperors gossiped here. So can you.

attractions.name: Pompeii
attractions.desc: A whole Roman city paused mid-bite by Vesuvius — streets, bakeries, 2,000-year-old graffiti fresher than your feed.

attractions.name: Mount Vesuvius
attractions.desc: Peer into the crater that made Pompeii famous. Still technically awake, which makes the hike deliciously dramatic.

attractions.name: National Archaeological Museum
attractions.desc: Where Pompeii's best stuff actually lives — mosaics, bronzes, and one room the Victorians deemed too spicy.

attractions.name: Spaccanapoli
attractions.desc: The straight-line street that slices old Naples in two. Laundry overhead, scooters everywhere, drama included free.

attractions.name: Castel dell'Ovo
attractions.desc: A sea castle allegedly balanced on a magic egg. If the egg breaks, Naples falls. No pressure. Bay views: free.

attractions.name: Galleria Umberto I
attractions.desc: A glass-domed shopping cathedral where doing absolutely nothing feels expensive. It isn't.

attractions.name: Napoli Sotterranea
attractions.desc: Forty meters under the pizza: Greek-Roman tunnels and WWII shelters. Bring curiosity, leave claustrophobia at street level.

attractions.name: Piazza del Plebiscito
attractions.desc: A vast stone stage where kids play football between royal colonnades. Naples' living room, no cover charge.

attractions.name: Lungomare Caracciolo
attractions.desc: Sunset seafront stroll with Vesuvius posing across the bay. The whole postcard, zero euros.

attractions.name: San Gregorio Armeno
attractions.desc: The alley where artisans carve tiny popes and footballers for nativity scenes all year. Christmas never checks out here.

attractions.name: Asinelli Tower
attractions.desc: 498 wooden steps up a medieval skyscraper that leans just enough to be interesting. Reward: a sea of red roofs.

attractions.name: Piazza Maggiore
attractions.desc: Bologna's front porch — giant basilica, summer open-air cinema, endless loitering. Sit on the crescentone and just be.

attractions.name: Basilica di San Petronio
attractions.desc: So big they ran out of money for the facade — half marble, half brick, all charm. Free to gawk.

attractions.name: Archiginnasio & Anatomical Theatre
attractions.desc: The old university's crest-crusted halls plus a carved wooden theatre where anatomy got theatrical. Pocket-change entry.

attractions.name: Portico di San Luca
attractions.desc: 666 arches marching uphill to a sanctuary — the world's longest portico and a free cardio pilgrimage with a view.

attractions.name: Quadrilatero Market
attractions.desc: Medieval lanes stacked with mortadella, fresh pasta and unapologetic cheese. Window-licking costs nothing.

attractions.name: Basilica di Santo Stefano
attractions.desc: Seven churches nested like Russian dolls on one quiet piazza. A millennium of calm, zero entry fee.

attractions.name: Finestrella di Via Piella
attractions.desc: A hole in a wall revealing Bologna's secret canal. Thirty seconds of Venice, zero seconds of Venice prices.

attractions.name: Giardini Margherita
attractions.desc: The city's big green exhale — a lake, turtles, students pretending to study. Picnic-grade happiness.

attractions.name: MAMbo
attractions.desc: Bologna's modern-art house in an old industrial bakery. Morandi's quiet bottles will rewire your brain for pocket money.

attractions.name: Sagrada Família
attractions.desc: Gaudí's unfinished fever dream, 140 years in the making. Inside feels like standing in a stone forest at sunrise.

attractions.name: Park Güell
attractions.desc: A mosaic wonderland on a hill — gingerbread houses, a tiled lizard, and the whole city rolling down to the sea.

attractions.name: La Rambla
attractions.desc: A mile-long catwalk of human theatre. Hold your bag, slow your walk, drink it all in for free.

attractions.name: La Boqueria Market
attractions.desc: A market that politely assaults you with jamón, juice cones and octopus. Entry free; willpower expensive.

attractions.name: Gothic Quarter
attractions.desc: Roman walls, medieval alleys, plazas that appear out of nowhere. Get lost on purpose — that's the whole point.

attractions.name: Barceloneta Beach
attractions.desc: City sand, cheap and cheerful. Someone's playing guitar badly and the Mediterranean simply does not care.

attractions.name: Casa Batlló
attractions.desc: Gaudí's house of bones and dragon scales on a fancy boulevard. Pricey inside — but the facade show is a free stare.

attractions.name: Bunkers del Carmel
attractions.desc: Old anti-aircraft bunkers turned the city's best 360° sunset couch. BYO snacks and someone to nudge at golden hour.

attractions.name: Montjuïc
attractions.desc: A castle-topped hill of gardens and museums staring down the port. Wander up for free, descend feeling smug.

attractions.name: Picasso Museum
attractions.desc: Teen Picasso's homework through blue-period genius, spread over five medieval palaces. Free slots exist if you time it.

attractions.name: Museo del Prado
attractions.desc: Velázquez, Goya and Bosch's nightmares under one roof. Free entry the last two hours daily — the broke traveler cheat code.

attractions.name: El Retiro Park
attractions.desc: Madrid's backyard: row a boat past a glass palace, dodge rollerbladers, nap like royalty under very old trees.

attractions.name: Royal Palace
attractions.desc: Europe's biggest royal pad by floor space — thousands of chandelier-heavy rooms. The kings moved out; the swagger stayed.

attractions.name: Plaza Mayor
attractions.desc: A 400-year-old square that's hosted markets, fiestas and worse. Coffee costs triple here; standing costs nothing.

attractions.name: Puerta del Sol
attractions.desc: Kilometre Zero of all Spain. Touch the plaque, find the bear statue, feel briefly like the center of everything.

attractions.name: Reina Sofía Museum
attractions.desc: Home of Picasso's Guernica — a wall-sized gut punch. Free evening slots exist for dreamers on a budget.

attractions.name: Mercado de San Miguel
attractions.desc: A glass jewel box of tapas counters. Walk in free, inhale the jamón air, budget for one perfect bite.

attractions.name: Templo de Debod
attractions.desc: An actual Egyptian temple, gifted to Madrid, glowing at dusk. The most exotic free sunset in the city.

attractions.name: Gran Vía
attractions.desc: Madrid's Broadway — rooftop bars, giant billboards, buildings that dress up at night. Neck cranes are free.

attractions.name: El Rastro Flea Market
attractions.desc: Sunday flea-market chaos tumbling downhill — vinyl, antiques, treasure, junk. The haggling counts as cardio.

attractions.name: La Concha Beach
attractions.desc: A crescent of sand so perfect it feels rented from a postcard. Costs nothing to stand there plotting the rest of your life.

attractions.name: Monte Igueldo
attractions.desc: Rattly 1912 funicular to a fairground stuck in time, with the best bay view money barely buys. Bring a few coins and some vertigo.

attractions.name: Monte Urgull
attractions.desc: Free hilltop hike past old cannons to a giant statue watching the surf roll in. The city's cheapest throne.

attractions.name: Peine del Viento
attractions.desc: Rusted steel combs bolted into rocks where waves explode. On stormy nights the ground hisses under you. Free, feral, unforgettable.

attractions.name: San Telmo Museoa
attractions.desc: Basque history tucked into a 16th-century convent. A few bucks to understand why this tiny city out-eats everyone.

attractions.name: Aquarium Donostia
attractions.desc: Walk a glass tunnel while sharks commute overhead. Old-school, harborside, and worth skipping two pintxos for.

attractions.name: Zurriola Beach
attractions.desc: The surfy, scruffy beach across the river where Gros kids paddle out at dawn. Free front-row seats to other people's wipeouts.

attractions.name: Miramar Palace Gardens
attractions.desc: Royal lawns strung between the two beaches. Bring bread, cheese, and delusions of aristocracy — the view is included.

attractions.name: Buen Pastor Cathedral
attractions.desc: The neo-gothic spire anchoring the skyline. Slip in for quiet and stained glass; the price of awe here is zero.

attractions.name: Plaza de la Constitución
attractions.desc: Numbered balconies left over from its bullring days. Order one drink, hold the table, watch the old town do its thing.

attractions.name: Belém Tower
attractions.desc: A little stone fortress standing in the river like it forgot the empire ended. A few euros to climb inside a postcard.

attractions.name: Jerónimos Monastery
attractions.desc: Stone carved so fine it looks piped like frosting. Sailors prayed here before sailing off the map. The church part is free.

attractions.name: Praça do Comércio
attractions.desc: A yellow royal square that opens straight onto the river. Free sunsets the size of an empire's ego.

attractions.name: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
attractions.desc: The lookout locals climb at golden hour. Whole city, castle, river — free, plus whatever the guy with the cooler charges.

attractions.name: São Jorge Castle
attractions.desc: Moorish walls with peacocks on patrol. Pay up, walk the ramparts, pretend the terracotta sprawl below is all yours.

attractions.name: Tram 28
attractions.desc: A rickety yellow rollercoaster disguised as public transit. Cheapest city tour in Europe, if you can snag a seat.

attractions.name: LX Factory
attractions.desc: Old factories under the big red bridge, now bookstores, murals, and food stalls. Browsing ambition is free.

attractions.name: Oceanário de Lisboa
attractions.desc: One giant tank where sunfish drift by like slow planets. Pricey — file it under rainy-day someday splurge.

attractions.name: Santa Justa Lift
attractions.desc: A wrought-iron elevator from 1902 that hoists you over the rooftops. Or hack it: walk up the hill behind for the same view.

attractions.name: Alfama Old Town Walk
attractions.desc: Laundry-strung alleys older than the maps. Get lost on purpose; the fado leaking from doorways is free.

attractions.name: Tivoli Gardens
attractions.desc: The 1843 amusement park that inspired Disney, with better lighting. Entry stings, but the evening glow is noodles-for-a-week worthy.

attractions.name: Nyhavn
attractions.desc: The candy-colored harbor from every screensaver. Skip the quayside menus, grab something cheap, sit on the edge like a local.

attractions.name: The Little Mermaid
attractions.desc: She's small, she's mobbed, she's free. Go at 7am and you and the bronze girl can be quietly wistful together.

attractions.name: Rosenborg Castle
attractions.desc: A fairytale castle guarding the actual crown jewels. Pay to peek at royal loot; the Kongens Have lawns outside are free.

attractions.name: Freetown Christiania
attractions.desc: The self-declared freetown of murals and workshops. Free to wander, wild to explain to your parents. Mind the no-photo zones.

attractions.name: Rundetaarn
attractions.desc: A 1642 tower climbed by spiral ramp — a king once rode a horse up it. A few bucks for skyline plus smug historical trivia.

attractions.name: Torvehallerne
attractions.desc: Twin glass halls of smørrebrød and pastry. Free to enter, dangerous to your last hundred kroner.

attractions.name: Superkilen
attractions.desc: A park striped red and black, furnished with objects from 60 countries. Skate, swing, people-watch — all free.

attractions.name: Amalienborg Palace Square
attractions.desc: Four palaces around one octagonal square. Catch the changing of the guard at noon for free royal theater.

attractions.name: Botanical Garden
attractions.desc: Victorian glasshouses and free jungle air downtown. The palm house is the cheapest tropical vacation in Denmark.

attractions.name: Rijksmuseum
attractions.desc: Rembrandts down a golden hallway. Steep ticket, but the gardens and the bike tunnel straight through the building are free.

attractions.name: Van Gogh Museum
attractions.desc: The world's biggest stash of a guy who sold one painting while alive. Book ahead; leave weirdly hopeful about your own hustle.

attractions.name: Anne Frank House
attractions.desc: The hidden annex behind the bookcase. Book weeks out. Small rooms, low ceilings, and a quiet that stays with you.

attractions.name: Vondelpark
attractions.desc: Amsterdam's green living room. Free roses, free people-watching, herons auditing your picnic.

attractions.name: Canal Ring Cruise
attractions.desc: An hour gliding under crooked bridges past crooked houses. Touristy? Sure. Also the city's single best angle.

attractions.name: Albert Cuyp Market
attractions.desc: The country's longest street market. Warm stroopwafels pressed in front of you — grazing here is a lifestyle.

attractions.name: Jordaan Canal Walk
attractions.desc: Once working-class, now the prettiest maze of canals and hidden courtyards. Wandering is free; wanting to live here costs everything.

attractions.name: A'DAM Lookout
attractions.desc: Rooftop deck with a swing that dangles you over the harbor's edge. Pay to scream photogenically.

attractions.name: Bloemenmarkt
attractions.desc: A floating flower market since 1862. Tulip bulbs, questionable souvenirs, and free color therapy.

attractions.name: NDSM Wharf
attractions.desc: A shipyard turned street-art playground across the water. The ferry over is free, which honestly feels illegal.

attractions.name: Schönbrunn Palace
attractions.desc: 1,441 rooms of Habsburg excess. The gardens and Gloriette hill are free — climb up and pity emperors with worse views than yours.

attractions.name: St. Stephen's Cathedral
attractions.desc: The tiled-roof cathedral at Vienna's dead center. Standing in the nave costs nothing; the shiver is complimentary.

attractions.name: Belvedere Palace
attractions.desc: Baroque palace holding Klimt's golden Kiss. One ticket to see the most famous hug in art history.

attractions.name: Prater & Riesenrad
attractions.desc: Free-entry park with an 1897 ferris wheel spinning slow-motion movie history. Ride it someday; loiter beneath it tonight.

attractions.name: Naschmarkt
attractions.desc: A mile of stalls — olives, cheese, Saturday flea-market chaos. Grazing the free samples is basically a Viennese sport.

attractions.name: Kunsthistorisches Museum
attractions.desc: Bruegel, Vermeer, and a marble stairwell built to humble you. The café under the dome might be Europe's prettiest room.

attractions.name: Stadtpark
attractions.desc: Home of the golden Strauss statue, frozen mid-waltz. Free lawns, free swans, free soundtrack in your head.

attractions.name: Vienna State Opera
attractions.desc: World-class opera with standing tickets for pocket change. Stand tall and absorb high culture at kebab prices.

attractions.name: Hofburg Palace
attractions.desc: The Habsburgs' winter HQ — imperial apartments, Sisi's story, and enough chandeliers to cover your rent for years.

attractions.name: Donauinsel
attractions.desc: A 21 km river island of beaches, grill spots and bike paths. Vienna's free summer resort — no reservation required.

attractions.name: Acropolis of Athens
attractions.desc: The OG skyline flex, 2,400 years running. Go at dawn, beat the heat, and pretend the Parthenon was built just for your someday montage.

attractions.name: Acropolis Museum
attractions.desc: Glass floors over ancient streets and marbles staring right back at you. Cheaper than therapy, older than everything you own.

attractions.name: Monastiraki Flea Market
attractions.desc: Sunday chaos of vinyl, brass lamps and maybe-real antiques under the Acropolis. Haggling is free and the people-watching is priceless.

attractions.name: Lycabettus Hill
attractions.desc: Huff up the pine path at sunset and watch Athens glow orange all the way to the sea. Costs zero, feels like a movie ending.

attractions.name: Temple of Olympian Zeus
attractions.desc: A handful of colossal columns that took 600 years to finish. Proof your side project timeline is fine, honestly.

attractions.name: Panathenaic Stadium
attractions.desc: All-marble stadium where the first modern Olympics ran. Sprint the track, climb the podium, collect your imaginary gold.

attractions.name: National Garden
attractions.desc: Shady escape hatch behind Parliament — palms, turtles, free-roaming ducks. The cheapest reset button in the city.

attractions.name: Ancient Agora
attractions.desc: Where Socrates cornered strangers with questions. Wander the old marketplace and get philosophical for pocket change.

attractions.name: Anafiotika
attractions.desc: A tiny island village smuggled onto the Acropolis slope. Whitewashed lanes, sleepy cats, zero entry fee, maximum daydream.

attractions.name: Hagia Sophia
attractions.desc: 1,500 years of empires arguing over the same dome. Stand under it once and your group chat will hear about it forever.

attractions.name: Blue Mosque
attractions.desc: Six minarets and a ceiling of blue tiles that will crane your neck the good way. Free — dress modest and drift in.

attractions.name: Topkapi Palace
attractions.desc: Sultans' quarters, emerald daggers and harem gossip fossilized in tile. Steep ticket, but it is basically time travel.

attractions.name: Grand Bazaar
attractions.desc: 4,000 shops of lamps, rugs and tea-fueled negotiation. Enter broke, leave broke but carrying excellent stories.

attractions.name: Spice Bazaar
attractions.desc: Pyramids of saffron, lokum and pepper perfume the air at no charge. Sniffing is on the house; willpower not included.

attractions.name: Galata Tower
attractions.desc: Medieval lookout with the postcard shot of the Golden Horn. Pricey lift, but sunset up here files firmly under someday-worthy.

attractions.name: Basilica Cistern
attractions.desc: An underground forest of columns with two Medusa heads doing headstands. Moody, drippy, gloriously weird.

attractions.name: Bosphorus Public Ferry
attractions.desc: Two continents, one glass of tea, a squad of seagulls — for about a dollar. The best cheap thrill in Istanbul, full stop.

attractions.name: Istiklal Street
attractions.desc: A red tram sliding through a river of three million people. Window-shop, snack, repeat — the city's free treadmill.

attractions.name: Süleymaniye Mosque
attractions.desc: Sinan's masterpiece on the third hill, quieter than the Blue Mosque with a skyline view thrown in free. Sit, breathe, plot your future.

attractions.name: Old Jaffa Port
attractions.desc: A 4,000-year-old harbor where the stones out-age everyone's opinions. Sunset here costs nothing and fixes most moods.

attractions.name: Carmel Market
attractions.desc: Vendors yelling, strawberries flying, halva samples if you time it right. The soundtrack of Tel Aviv, free admission.

attractions.name: Jaffa Flea Market
attractions.desc: Rugs, vinyl and somebody's grandma's chandeliers spilling into the alleys. Treasure-hunt by day, bar-hop the same stalls by night.

attractions.name: Rothschild Boulevard
attractions.desc: Bauhaus buildings, coffee kiosks and scooters dodging dogs. The city's living room — stroll it like you already pay rent here.

attractions.name: Tel Aviv Museum of Art
attractions.desc: Angular concrete outside, Israeli masters and big moderns inside. Cool air and cooler art when the beach gets loud.

attractions.name: Hilton Beach
attractions.desc: Surfers, the crack of matkot paddles, and a dog beach next door. Salt water is free and so is the vitamin D.

attractions.name: Park HaYarkon
attractions.desc: Tel Aviv's green lung — rowboats, endless lawns, parrots heckling from the trees. Naps here count as sightseeing.

attractions.name: White City Bauhaus District
attractions.desc: A UNESCO stash of 4,000 Bauhaus buildings going golden at dusk. Architecture nerd-out with a zero-dollar entry fee.

attractions.name: Namal Tel Aviv (Old Port)
attractions.desc: A boardwalk built in wooden waves, sea spray included. Broke-friendly hangout engineering at its finest.

attractions.name: Pigeon Rocks (Raouche)
attractions.desc: Two sea stacks posing off Raouche like they know they're famous. The sunset cliff seats are free forever.

attractions.name: Corniche Beirut
attractions.desc: The seaside catwalk where all Beirut walks, jogs, fishes and flirts. Bring coffee, borrow the Mediterranean.

attractions.name: National Museum of Beirut
attractions.desc: Phoenician sarcophagi and mosaics that survived everything. A few bucks for 5,000 years — best deal in town.

attractions.name: Sursock Museum
attractions.desc: A white-and-stained-glass mansion stacked with Lebanese art. Free to enter, impossible to leave uninspired.

attractions.name: Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque
attractions.desc: Blue dome, golden minarets, downtown's centerpiece. Step in respectfully — no ticket needed.

attractions.name: Zaitunay Bay
attractions.desc: Yachts you can't afford beside a promenade you absolutely can. Window-shopping the sea costs nothing.

attractions.name: Jeita Grotto
attractions.desc: A cathedral of stalactites with an underground boat ride. Feels almost illegal how pretty it is.

attractions.name: Harissa (Our Lady of Lebanon)
attractions.desc: A cable car up to the giant white Lady watching the whole bay. This view will ruin your camera roll in the best way.

attractions.name: Byblos Old Town
attractions.desc: One of Earth's oldest continuously lived-in towns, a short hop up the coast. Crusader castle, fishing port, big feelings.

attractions.name: Burj Khalifa
attractions.desc: The planet's tallest flex. The observation deck stings, but craning up from the fountain plaza is free and neck-cracking.

attractions.name: The Dubai Fountain
attractions.desc: Water doing choreography to opera under the Burj every evening. Front-row spectacle for exactly zero dirhams.

attractions.name: Dubai Frame
attractions.desc: A giant golden picture frame — old Dubai out one side, sci-fi Dubai out the other. Cheap ticket, expensive view.

attractions.name: Gold Souk
attractions.desc: Windows dripping with more gold than most central banks. Gawking is free; dreaming is actively encouraged.

attractions.name: Al Fahidi Historical District
attractions.desc: Wind towers, coral-stone walls and hushed lanes from before the skyscrapers. Old Dubai on a broke traveler's budget.

attractions.name: JBR Beach
attractions.desc: Free sand, warm Gulf water, a wall of towers glittering behind the towels. Swim first — the prices can wait.

attractions.name: Museum of the Future
attractions.desc: The torus building wrapped in glowing calligraphy. Steep entry, but even circling the outside feels like the year 2071.

attractions.name: Dubai Miracle Garden
attractions.desc: 150 million flowers sculpted into castles and airplanes, in a desert. Extra? Absolutely. Worth a someday? Also yes.

attractions.name: Abra Ride on Dubai Creek
attractions.desc: A wooden boat across the Creek for about thirty cents. The oldest commute in town and the best fare you'll ever pay.

attractions.name: Dubai Marina Walk
attractions.desc: Seven kilometers of yachts, towers and late-night shawarma. Strut it after dark like your ship already came in.

attractions.name: Pyramids of Giza
attractions.desc: 4,500 years old and still the flex. Stand where pharaohs planned forever and feel your rent worries shrink to sand.

attractions.name: Grand Egyptian Museum
attractions.desc: Tut's gold under one colossal new roof. Save up, walk in broke, walk out feeling like a king's accountant.

attractions.name: Egyptian Museum (Tahrir)
attractions.desc: The dusty-pink OG on Tahrir — mummies, sarcophagi, and a century of gloriously packed halls.

attractions.name: Khan el-Khalili
attractions.desc: Lantern-lit maze of brass, spice, and haggling since the 1300s. Browsing is free; mint tea is basically mandatory.

attractions.name: Al-Azhar Park
attractions.desc: A green hill over old Cairo for the price of a candy bar. Sunset plus a thousand minarets — cheapest cinema in town.

attractions.name: Citadel of Saladin
attractions.desc: A hilltop fortress with an alabaster mosque and a skyline that runs all the way to the pyramids on a clear day.

attractions.name: Cairo Tower
attractions.desc: Lotus-shaped 60s tower over the Nile. Go at night and count the city lights you can't afford yet.

attractions.name: Nile Corniche
attractions.desc: The riverside stroll every Cairene knows. Feluccas drift by, tea vendors appear, and nobody charges you for the moon.

attractions.name: Al-Muizz Street
attractions.desc: A kilometer of Fatimid Cairo lit up like an open-air museum after dark. Free time travel, batteries not required.

attractions.name: Coptic Cairo
attractions.desc: The Hanging Church, hushed lanes, and two thousand years stacked in layers — all before lunch.

attractions.name: Jemaa el-Fnaa
attractions.desc: The square that becomes a nightly circus — drummers, storytellers, orange juice for pennies. Broke-friendly since forever.

attractions.name: Jardin Majorelle
attractions.desc: That electric-blue garden all over your feed. Cacti, YSL lore, and shade genuinely worth saving for.

attractions.name: Bahia Palace
attractions.desc: Room after room of carved cedar and zellige built purely to drop jaws. Yours included.

attractions.name: Koutoubia Mosque
attractions.desc: The 12th-century minaret the whole city navigates by. Sunset from the rose gardens costs exactly nothing.

attractions.name: Ben Youssef Madrasa
attractions.desc: A 16th-century student dorm that out-decorates every palace hotel. The courtyard is a someday-list classic.

attractions.name: Saadian Tombs
attractions.desc: Royal tombs hidden behind a wall for centuries, dripping in marble and gold leaf. Secrets keep well here.

attractions.name: Le Jardin Secret
attractions.desc: An Islamic garden tucked mid-souk — trickling water channels, real silence, and a tower over the rooftops.

attractions.name: Menara Gardens
attractions.desc: Olive groves, a pavilion, a still pool, and the Atlas floating behind it all. A free postcard you can walk into.

attractions.name: The Medina Souks
attractions.desc: Miles of lamps, leather, and rugs you'll haggle for someday. Getting gloriously lost is the actual attraction.

attractions.name: Table Mountain
attractions.desc: The flat-topped icon. Ride the cableway — or hike Platteklip for free and earn the entire city at your feet.

attractions.name: Lion's Head
attractions.desc: The sunrise-hike rite of passage. Two oceans, one spiral path, zero entry fee.

attractions.name: Boulders Beach
attractions.desc: Penguins. Actual wild penguins waddling past your toes, for roughly the price of a burger.

attractions.name: Kirstenbosch Gardens
attractions.desc: A botanical garden spilling down the mountainside, with a treetop walkway. Prime picnic-and-dream territory.

attractions.name: Robben Island
attractions.desc: The ferry to Mandela's cell, with former prisoners as guides. Heavy, humbling, and worth every saved rand.

attractions.name: Cape of Good Hope
attractions.desc: Cliffs, cheeky baboons, and that end-of-the-continent feeling where two oceans meet to gossip.

attractions.name: V&A Waterfront
attractions.desc: Harbour buzz, buskers, and giant food halls. Watching seals dodge yachts is free entertainment.

attractions.name: Bo-Kaap
attractions.desc: Candy-coloured houses on cobbled slopes with koesisters close by. Bring your camera, not your wallet.

attractions.name: Sea Point Promenade
attractions.desc: The city's shared front porch — joggers, dogs, and sunsets where the Atlantic shamelessly shows off.

attractions.name: Camps Bay Beach
attractions.desc: White sand with the Twelve Apostles looming behind you. The tan is free; the cocktails are not.

attractions.name: Osaka Castle
attractions.desc: A gold-trimmed castle on a moat with cherry trees for days. The park is free; the keep is pocket change.

attractions.name: Dotonbori
attractions.desc: A neon canyon of giant mechanical crabs and the running-man sign. The city's entire personality in one glowing strip.

attractions.name: Kuromon Ichiba Market
attractions.desc: Osaka's kitchen — grilled scallops, tuna cheeks, and free entry. Your nose does the spending for you.

attractions.name: Umeda Sky Building
attractions.desc: Twin towers holding a floating rooftop observatory. A night view that makes all that overtime feel almost worth it.

attractions.name: Shitennoji Temple
attractions.desc: One of Japan's oldest temples — 1,400 years of calm for less than a convenience-store coffee.

attractions.name: Shinsekai
attractions.desc: A retro neon time-warp thick with kushikatsu smoke. Remember: double-dipping the sauce is the only crime here.

attractions.name: Tsutenkaku Tower
attractions.desc: The scrappy little Eiffel of the south side. Rub Billiken's feet for luck — you'll need it, dreamer.

attractions.name: Sumiyoshi Taisha
attractions.desc: An ancient shrine with a drum-arched bridge steep enough to count as a tiny pilgrimage. Free blessings included.

attractions.name: Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan
attractions.desc: A whale shark doing slow laps around a building-sized tank. Certified date-night cheat code.

attractions.name: Universal Studios Japan
attractions.desc: Mario and wizards in one park. The splurge square on everyone's someday bingo card.

attractions.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
attractions.desc: Ten thousand vermilion gates climbing a mountain, open all night, totally free. Broke-traveler royalty.

attractions.name: Kinkaku-ji
attractions.desc: A pavilion wrapped in actual gold, doubled in its own pond. Costs less than the latte you'd sip describing it.

attractions.name: Kiyomizu-dera
attractions.desc: A wooden stage jutting over the maple canopy. In autumn it burns red and so does your camera roll.

attractions.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
attractions.desc: Green corridors that creak and hush in the wind. Go at dawn and you own the entire soundtrack.

attractions.name: Nishiki Market
attractions.desc: A 400-year-old food alley — pickles, skewers, matcha everything. Grazing absolutely counts as dinner.

attractions.name: Gion District
attractions.desc: Lantern-lit lanes where a geiko might glide past. Look, don't chase — the vibe itself is the ticket.

attractions.name: Philosopher's Path
attractions.desc: A canal-side stroll purpose-built for overthinking. Cherry blossoms in April, perfect quiet the rest of the year.

attractions.name: Ryoan-ji
attractions.desc: Fifteen rocks, raked gravel, and a silence that quietly rearranges your brain. Cheapest therapy in town.

attractions.name: Nijo Castle
attractions.desc: A shogun's palace with nightingale floors that chirp on purpose — a medieval intruder alarm you get to test.

attractions.name: Ginkaku-ji
attractions.desc: The 'silver' pavilion that never got its silver — and is somehow more beautiful for the broken promise.

attractions.name: Haeundae Beach
attractions.desc: Korea's most famous sand. Zero won to watch the sunrise with cup ramyeon while the whole city sleeps behind you.

attractions.name: Gamcheon Culture Village
attractions.desc: A hillside of candy-colored houses and alley art. Get lost on purpose — the wandering is free and so are the views.

attractions.name: Jagalchi Fish Market
attractions.desc: Auntie-run fish stalls the size of a small nation. Come for the chaos, stay pretending you'll splurge on king crab someday.

attractions.name: Haedong Yonggungsa Temple
attractions.desc: A temple perched right on the sea rocks. Waves crash, lanterns sway, wallet stays closed.

attractions.name: Gwangalli Beach & Gwangan Bridge
attractions.desc: The diamond bridge lights up at night like it knows you're watching. Best free light show in Busan.

attractions.name: Busan Tower
attractions.desc: Old-school tower above Nampo-dong. A few bucks buys you the whole glittering port at your feet.

attractions.name: Taejongdae Park
attractions.desc: Cliffs, pines, and a lighthouse at the edge of Korea. Entry: free. Feeling tiny in a good way: included.

attractions.name: Beomeosa Temple
attractions.desc: A 1,300-year-old mountain temple where the city noise finally shuts up. Free peace, bring your own questions.

attractions.name: Songdo Marine Cable Car
attractions.desc: Glass-floor cabins gliding over open sea. Save it for a someday flex — window seat over the waves.

attractions.name: Gukje Market
attractions.desc: A post-war market maze — vintage everything, street toast, and hotteok worth burning your mouth for.

attractions.name: Victoria Peak
attractions.desc: The skyline you've screenshotted a hundred times, from above it. Tram up, jaw down.

attractions.name: Star Ferry
attractions.desc: Cross the harbour for pocket change — the cheapest million-dollar view on Earth.

attractions.name: Temple Street Night Market
attractions.desc: Neon signs, fortune tellers, clay-pot rice steam. Window shopping counts as a full evening plan here.

attractions.name: Tian Tan Big Buddha
attractions.desc: A 34-meter bronze Buddha sitting above the Lantau clouds. The 268 steps are free; so is the calm.

attractions.name: Dragon's Back Trail
attractions.desc: A ridge hike with beach-and-sea views the whole way. Costs nothing but one very sweaty T-shirt.

attractions.name: Avenue of Stars
attractions.desc: Kowloon waterfront facing the flashiest skyline alive. At 8pm the buildings literally perform a free light show.

attractions.name: M+ Museum
attractions.desc: Asia's giant visual-culture museum in a building that looks beamed in from the future. Someday-ticket energy.

attractions.name: Wong Tai Sin Temple
attractions.desc: Incense smoke, fortune sticks, and roof dragons. Ask for luck — it's the one thing here with no price tag.

attractions.name: Ding Ding Tram Ride
attractions.desc: Rattle across the island on a double-decker tram for cents. Front seat upstairs is broke-budget first class.

attractions.name: Ocean Park
attractions.desc: Roller coasters on a cliff over the South China Sea. The when-payday-finally-hits kind of day out.

attractions.name: Taipei 101 Observatory
attractions.desc: Once the world's tallest, still the city's exclamation point. The observatory is future-you's treat.

attractions.name: Shilin Night Market
attractions.desc: A galaxy of sizzling stalls. Entry is free; willpower is not included.

attractions.name: Longshan Temple
attractions.desc: Incense coils, carved dragons, whispered wishes since 1738. Open late enough for your kind of hours.

attractions.name: Elephant Mountain
attractions.desc: Twenty sweaty minutes of stairs, then Taipei 101 framed in jungle. The classic free skyline shot.

attractions.name: National Palace Museum
attractions.desc: An emperors' treasure vault — jade cabbage included. A few bucks for five thousand years of loot.

attractions.name: Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall
attractions.desc: A vast white hall on a plaza built for wide-angle daydreams. Guard change on the hour, free of charge.

attractions.name: Beitou Thermal Valley
attractions.desc: A steaming jade-green spring that looks borrowed from another planet. Staring is free; soaking nearby is cheap.

attractions.name: Maokong Gondola
attractions.desc: Glass-bottom cabins floating over tea plantations for pocket change. Mountain teahouses wait at the top.

attractions.name: Raohe Street Night Market
attractions.desc: One glorious street of pepper buns and neon. The temple at the gate practically blesses your appetite.

attractions.name: Tamsui Old Street
attractions.desc: Riverside snacks at the end of the metro line. Locals swear the sun sets better out here — go check their math.

attractions.name: Ben Thanh Market
attractions.desc: The clock-tower market where all of Saigon haggles. Browse like you're rich, snack like you're smart.

attractions.name: War Remnants Museum
attractions.desc: Heavy, necessary, unforgettable — and it costs about as much as an iced coffee.

attractions.name: Independence Palace
attractions.desc: A 1960s time capsule with war rooms in the basement and a helicopter parked on the roof.

attractions.name: Saigon Central Post Office
attractions.desc: A honey-colored colonial hall where you can still mail a someday-postcard to future you.

attractions.name: Jade Emperor Pagoda
attractions.desc: A smoke-dark pagoda full of carved gods and resident turtles. Quietly one of the city's best free wonders.

attractions.name: Nguyen Hue Walking Street
attractions.desc: Saigon's living room after dark — fountains, skate kids, and everyone out chasing the evening breeze.

attractions.name: Bitexco Saigon Skydeck
attractions.desc: The lotus-shaped tower with the helipad ledge. One ticket buys the whole motorbike galaxy swirling below.

attractions.name: Thien Hau Temple
attractions.desc: Cholon's sea-goddess temple under a slow rain of incense coils. Wishes hang from the ceiling, literally.

attractions.name: Landmark 81 SkyView
attractions.desc: Vietnam's tallest tower — pure someday-list material. Even from the riverside park it steals the skyline.

attractions.name: Tao Dan Park
attractions.desc: Old trees, dawn tai chi, and the famous morning corner where uncles bring their songbirds to brunch.

attractions.name: Hoan Kiem Lake
attractions.desc: The turtle-legend lake at the city's heart. One free lap at midnight fixes most moods.

attractions.name: Old Quarter
attractions.desc: Thirty-six ancient streets, each named for what it once sold. Wandering them IS the attraction.

attractions.name: Hanoi Train Street
attractions.desc: A real train squeezes past café stools a few times a day. Cheap coffee, front-row adrenaline.

attractions.name: Temple of Literature
attractions.desc: Vietnam's thousand-year-old first university. A few bucks to walk where scholars once sweated their exams.

attractions.name: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
attractions.desc: Solemn granite, silent guards, free entry. Dress like you're meeting someone's strict grandfather.

attractions.name: Tran Quoc Pagoda
attractions.desc: A 1,500-year-old red pagoda floating on West Lake. Sunset here is free and criminally photogenic.

attractions.name: Hoa Lo Prison Museum
attractions.desc: The infamous 'Hanoi Hilton.' Sobering history for pocket change.

attractions.name: Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre
attractions.desc: Puppets dancing on water to live folk music — a thousand-year-old art for cheap-seat money.

attractions.name: Dong Xuan Market
attractions.desc: The Old Quarter's mothership market. Come for the fabric mountains, stay for the food alley out back.

attractions.name: Long Bien Bridge
attractions.desc: A century-old iron bridge over the Red River. Walk it at dawn as trains rattle past banana groves below.

attractions.name: Kek Lok Si Temple
attractions.desc: Hillside mega-temple stacking pagodas like it's showing off. During lantern season it glows so hard your camera roll taps out.

attractions.name: Penang Hill
attractions.desc: Ride the funicular up, watch George Town shrink into fairy lights, eat overpriced ice cream anyway. The cool air up top is free.

attractions.name: George Town Street Art Trail
attractions.desc: Free scavenger hunt through heritage lanes — kids on bicycle murals, cats, swings. Your whole feed for zero ringgit.

attractions.name: Chew Jetty
attractions.desc: A wooden clan village on stilts over the sea, still lived-in. Sunset here costs nothing and looks like a million bucks.

attractions.name: Cheong Fatt Tze Blue Mansion
attractions.desc: An indigo courtyard mansion so photogenic it's been in movies. Tour it once, redecorate your imaginary house forever.

attractions.name: Penang National Park
attractions.desc: Tiny national park, huge flex: jungle trail out to a turtle beach and a canopy walk. Basically a free adventure movie.

attractions.name: Batu Ferringhi Beach
attractions.desc: Long sandy stretch where the night market rolls out as the sun drops. Haggle a little, snack a lot, sleep happy.

attractions.name: Gurney Drive Promenade
attractions.desc: Seafront strip where hawker legends work the woks after dark. Wok steam plus sea breeze equals the perfect broke night out.

attractions.name: Penang Botanic Gardens
attractions.desc: Monkey-patrolled green escape locals call the Waterfall Gardens. Free morning walks, judgmental macaques included.

attractions.name: Fort Cornwallis
attractions.desc: Star-shaped fort from 1786 with cannons still eyeing the strait. Cheap history, sea views, zero gym membership required.

attractions.name: Petronas Twin Towers
attractions.desc: Twin steel rockets tied together with a skybridge. Stand below at night for free and feel very, very small in the best way.

attractions.name: Batu Caves
attractions.desc: 272 rainbow steps up to a cave temple, guarded by a golden giant and monkeys with zero manners. Free, but bring leg-day energy.

attractions.name: KL Tower
attractions.desc: The other tower — arguably the better view, because this skyline includes the Petronas. The sunset slot is the move.

attractions.name: Merdeka Square
attractions.desc: Where independence was declared under a 95-metre flagpole. A free lap of history past the fanciest old buildings in town.

attractions.name: Petaling Street Market
attractions.desc: Chinatown's covered bazaar — haggling is the cardio, the snack stalls are the reward. Entry free, willpower extra.

attractions.name: KLCC Park
attractions.desc: Manicured lawns with a fountain show dancing under the twin towers every night. Free front-row seats to a light symphony.

attractions.name: Islamic Arts Museum Malaysia
attractions.desc: Domes, calligraphy and miniature mosques in a serene white building. A few bucks buys some of the calmest beauty in the city.

attractions.name: Thean Hou Temple
attractions.desc: Six tiers of red lanterns and dragons on a hilltop. Free, glowing, and basically built for your someday photo album.

attractions.name: Jalan Alor Food Street
attractions.desc: One street, a hundred woks, all fired up after dark. Come broke, leave full — this is KL's real night show.

attractions.name: Perdana Botanical Gardens
attractions.desc: KL's oldest garden — lakes, hibiscus and shade for days. The city's free reset button since 1888.

attractions.name: Gateway of India
attractions.desc: A stone arch by the harbour that watched an empire leave. Sea spray, pigeons, boat horns — the classic Mumbai hello, free forever.

attractions.name: Marine Drive
attractions.desc: The Queen's Necklace: a curve of streetlights along the sea. Sit on the wall at midnight, count waves, fix your whole life. Free.

attractions.name: Elephanta Caves
attractions.desc: Ferry out to an island where giant Shiva sculptures were carved into rock 1,400 years ago. Absolute someday-list core.

attractions.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus
attractions.desc: A railway station dressed like a gothic palace — gargoyles, domes, two million commuters. The commute IS the museum.

attractions.name: Juhu Beach
attractions.desc: Sunset beach where the whole city shows up for sea air and snack-stall smoke. A free show every single evening.

attractions.name: Haji Ali Dargah
attractions.desc: A white shrine floating at the end of a causeway that vanishes at high tide. Timing is everything; entry is nothing.

attractions.name: Crawford Market
attractions.desc: A Victorian market hall buzzing with mangoes, spices and chaos in the best possible ratio. Window-shopping smells amazing here.

attractions.name: Sanjay Gandhi National Park
attractions.desc: An actual leopard-holding national park inside city limits, plus 2,000-year-old cave monasteries. Under a buck to enter.

attractions.name: Hanging Gardens
attractions.desc: Terraced gardens on Malabar Hill with hedge animals and sunsets over the whole bay. Old-school, free, quietly elite.

attractions.name: Chor Bazaar
attractions.desc: The legendary 'thieves market' — gramophones, brass, old film posters. Treasure hunting is free; leaving empty-handed is hard.

attractions.name: Red Fort
attractions.desc: Massive red sandstone walls that once ran an empire. Walk where emperors schemed, then exit straight into Old Delhi's snack gauntlet.

attractions.name: India Gate
attractions.desc: A war memorial arch with lawns where half of Delhi turns up for evening ice cream. Free, floodlit, iconic.

attractions.name: Qutub Minar
attractions.desc: A 73-metre victory tower from 1193 still out-flexing every skyscraper on style. The carved ruins around it are the bonus level.

attractions.name: Humayun's Tomb
attractions.desc: The garden tomb that inspired the Taj Mahal — quieter, redder, closer. Golden hour here feels illegal at this price.

attractions.name: Lotus Temple
attractions.desc: A giant marble lotus where everyone's welcome and it costs nothing. The silence inside hits different after Delhi traffic.

attractions.name: Chandni Chowk
attractions.desc: A 400-year-old market maze — jalebi stands, paratha lanes, rickshaws playing bumper cars. Bring an appetite, not a plan.

attractions.name: Lodhi Gardens
attractions.desc: Crumbling 15th-century tombs scattered through jogger-filled gardens. Picnic among dynasties for exactly zero rupees.

attractions.name: Jama Masjid
attractions.desc: One of India's grandest mosques — climb a minaret and Old Delhi unrolls beneath you like a map. Entry free, views priceless.

attractions.name: Akshardham Temple
attractions.desc: A carved sandstone mega-temple so detailed it doesn't look real. Free to enter, impossible to fit on a postcard.

attractions.name: Hauz Khas Complex
attractions.desc: Medieval fort ruins on a lake, right beside boutique cafés — study the 14th century, then people-watch the 21st. Free.

attractions.name: Queen Victoria Market
attractions.desc: A city block of cheese, doughnuts and bargain fruit under heritage sheds since 1878. Sample your way to full.

attractions.name: Hosier Lane
attractions.desc: The famous ever-changing graffiti lane — new masterpieces sprayed over old ones weekly. Free gallery, open 24/7.

attractions.name: Royal Botanic Gardens
attractions.desc: 38 hectares of lakes, lawns and black swans one tram-hop from the CBD. Nature's free co-working space.

attractions.name: Federation Square
attractions.desc: The angular plaza everyone loves to argue about — big screens, buskers, free wifi and prime people-watching by the Yarra.

attractions.name: St Kilda Pier Penguins
attractions.desc: Wild little penguins waddle home to the breakwater at dusk. A zero-dollar wildlife documentary, filmed live nightly.

attractions.name: Melbourne Cricket Ground
attractions.desc: The 100,000-seat cathedral of sport. Tour the hallowed turf, or just soak up the roar from outside on game day.

attractions.name: National Gallery of Victoria
attractions.desc: Australia's oldest gallery, water-wall entrance included. The permanent collection costs exactly nothing.

attractions.name: Melbourne Skydeck
attractions.desc: 88 floors up with the whole glittering grid of Melbourne stretching to the horizon. Save it for a payday sunset.

attractions.name: Luna Park
attractions.desc: A 1912 seaside fair you enter through a giant grinning mouth. Wandering in is free; the heritage rides are the splurge.

attractions.name: Flinders Street Station
attractions.desc: The mustard-yellow station with the domed clocks — 'meet me under the clocks' is a whole Melbourne love language. Free.
